relationship: A single linear scale factor changes corresponding lengths by that factor, areas by its square and volumes by its cube.

learnerLoop.action: Drag an edge, fill unit squares, build cube layers, commit a prediction before checking, scale a non-unit reference, and repair an unequal height.
learnerLoop.modelChange: Lengths, corresponding face area, and volume derive from k, k², and k²h. h = k for similarity.
learnerLoop.evidence: Unit tilings and cube layers precede the powers. A two-unit reference separates physical edge length from scale factor. Prediction verdicts appear only after testing.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Use the relationship for a reverse target, a counterexample, or a self-directed comparison.

invariants: Similar solids keep one common linear scale factor across corresponding edges.
Area and volume factors are respectively the square and cube of that factor.
safeAdaptations: Vary positive scale factors and prototype dimensions.
Adjust working support while preserving the linked length, area and volume representations.
nonGoals: Applying the linear scale factor directly to area or volume.

prompt.description: A visually identified current mission, with context connecting the previous experience to the next action.

model.description: Lengths, corresponding face area, and volume derive from k, k², and k²h. h = k for similarity.
model.visibility: Always visible; later controls are progressively disclosed.

help.description: Learner-requested evidence cue, relationship hint and contrasting worked example; no automatic answer-directed pulse.
help.visibility: Only when requested in the relevant experience.

comparison.description: Frozen readings and explicitly labelled comparison conditions; graphical overlays use the selected saved reading.

navigation.description: Back and Forward restore snapshots; Repeat resets the current experience; Start over clears the session.
navigation.visibility: Back and Forward depend on visited progress.

working.description: Worked examples precede learner calculations. Explicit quantity keys connect source labels to formula operands, with matching highlights and a button-triggered trace. Hover, focus and tap explain each source and calculation.

evidence.description: Unit tilings and cube layers precede the powers. A two-unit reference separates physical edge length from scale factor. Prediction verdicts appear only after testing.
evidence.visibility: In-place feedback; readings only in relevant steps.

completion.description: New progression uses a model-derived criterion; previously visited experiences can be inspected without repeating them.
completion.visibility: Guided steps; absent in the open experiment.

scale.domain: 0.5 to 3 guided; 0.5 to 5 in the experiment, in steps of 0.1.
scale.output: Edge, face grid, cube grid and factor labels.

height.description: Independent height factor h for the non-similar counterexample.
height.domain: 0.5 to 3 guided; 0.5 to 5 in the experiment.

modes.guided: Small ordered visual investigations, with model actions and in-place revision.
modes.experiment: Ungated experiment: change view, separate layers, alter height, record immutable readings and select a comparison outline; returning restores the entire experiment.

dependencies: Build two layers, four cubes each.
Predict k = 3 from area factor 9, resize independently, then explicitly test; typing never grades the answer and edits invalidate success.
Use an original edge of 2 and original volume 8 to produce volume 64. Predict k = 2, resize, then test; the method is available through optional evidence-first hints.
Restore the height to match the two other edge ratios.
Ungated experiment: change view, separate layers, alter height, record immutable readings and select a comparison outline; returning restores the entire experiment.
implementation.completion: New experiences require their model-derived criterion. Back and Forward revisit saved state without forcing a rerun; Repeat experience resets only that experience. Start over clears all session snapshots. Worked observations are not mastery claims.
limitations: Introductory reference edge 1; the reverse-volume transfer uses reference edge 2 and volume 8. Face area means one corresponding face, not total surface area.
Continuous positive factors include partial units; all three powers apply only when h = k.
